summary.headline: Unicommerce Q2 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR59.1 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 17% from 22.2%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY to INR59.1 crore in Q2 FY27, with both Uniware and Shipway growing double digits. Adjusted EBITDA fell to INR10 crore (17% margin) from INR11.4 crore (22.2%) as management front-loaded investments in AI-led product, talent, and sales and marketing. PAT rose to INR6.4 crore from INR5.8 crore, helped by deferred tax recognition. Management guided that investment pace moderates in H2 FY27, with Shipway reaching adjusted EBITDA break-even in Q3 and PAT profitability in Q4.

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balances (end Q2 FY27)

segments.name: Uniware
segments.commentary: Added 121 enterprise clients in Q2 FY27 vs 103 a year earlier (+17.5%). International is about 6% of Uniware revenue, up from about 3% at listing, and is profitable. UniReco and UniCapture run-rate exceeds INR3 crore (about 2.5% of Uniware revenue), used by more than 150 clients.

segments.name: Shipway
segments.commentary: Grew more than 15% YoY and crossed INR100 crore annualised revenue run rate. Estimated market share is below 5% of a roughly INR4,000 crore courier aggregation market. Guided to adjusted EBITDA break-even from Q3 FY27 and PAT profitability from Q4 FY27.

segments.name: ConvertWay
segments.commentary: Mentioned only as a marketing solution in the cross-sell portfolio; no separate financials disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Uniware revenue growth above 15% YoY from Q4 FY27 onwards.
Shipway revenue growth to accelerate to above 20% YoY from Q4 FY27 onwards.
Shipway adjusted EBITDA break-even from Q3 FY27 and PAT profitability from Q4 FY27.
Incremental investment pace to moderate in H2 FY27, with consolidated profitability and margins expected to improve.
Long-term: grow business 5x in five years, with adjusted EBITDA margin returning to 20%+ at steady state (currently about 15-17%).
UniReco and UniCapture expected to exceed 10% of Uniware revenue over the next two to three years.
capex_capacity: Platform handled INR60 lakh transactions on a single day at Diwali peak with no issues; quick commerce peak processing doubled.
Launched DNA, a second-generation AI companion in Uniware; currently in beta with 10-15 customers and offered free, monetisation to follow.
Client onboarding rose to 120-150 per quarter from 85-90 at listing.
Investments in people, product and market reach were front-loaded in FY27; Shipway integration completed over the last 3-4 quarters.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per account (ARPA) fell in H1 FY27 by about 5% YoY per the analyst; management cited quarterly ARPA of about INR2.4 lakh in Q2 FY27 vs INR2.9 lakh in Q2 FY26, attributing this to long-tail clients who take 6-9 months to ramp.

B2B and quick commerce are used by 45-50% of the client base; management said per-transaction realisation is not like-for-like because bulk items carry lower realisation per item. B2C realisation stated as stable.
Module pricing still being discovered; combined UniReco and UniCapture could lift realisation to 1.5x-1.7x for adopting Uniware clients, with management expecting stabilisation at 1.2x-1.3x.
Attach rates: UniReco 7-8% and UniCapture 5-6% of Uniware enterprise clients.
Shipway cross-sell: about 10% client overlap with Uniware, yet 20-25% of Shipway shipment volumes come from Uniware clients.

Courier aggregation market is structured with one leader holding 20-25% share and about 45 fragmented players; management claims Unicommerce plus Shipway is the only player with a comprehensive suite.
Management said Uniware gross margin is around 80% and Shipway gross margin around 20%, in line with industry benchmarks.

qa_highlights.question: Why is average realisation per order declining despite enterprise client growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said B2B and quick commerce (used by 45-50% of clients) lower per-item realisation, so the metric is not like-for-like; it does not track rate per transaction and tracks NRR, new client adds and profit instead.

qa_highlights.question: Was the employee cost step-up proactive or overdue, given reports of tech stack issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the investments proactive, tied to AI, and said the platform is mission-critical with a 50% price premium; it disputed the tech stack criticism and cited 2x quick commerce peak processing growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H1 tax expense much lower on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to recognising deferred tax on expected tax benefits linked to Shipway turning profitable from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-5 year plan and when can margin reach 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 5x revenue growth over five years with adjusted EBITDA margin returning to 20%+ at steady state; the CFO said Uniware margin is 36% and consolidated is 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A planned, given the rise in current investments?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said current and non-current investments should be read together, as the gap is largely fixed deposits maturing within 12 months. CEO said M&A must meet four criteria (customer fit, good product and team, profitable or path to profit, reasonable valuation) and there is no fixed timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Does the market size support Shipway's growth and what is the right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a INR4,000 crore courier aggregation market, a 20-25% leader, and right to win from the OMS/WMS suite, sticky Uniware cross-sell and a service-first approach; D2C market growing in double digits.

risks_watch: Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed 520 bps YoY to 17%; delivery of Q3-Q4 margin recovery depends on moderating investment and Shipway break-even.
Declining ARPA: long-tail client mix and B2B/quick commerce dilution; watch whether ARPA stabilises near INR2.4 lakh per quarter.
Shipway PAT profitability from Q4 FY27 relies partly on deferred tax recognition; cash tax benefit uncertain.
DNA AI product is free in beta; monetisation timing and pricing are unclear.
M&A: management has been signalling deals for several quarters without a concrete announcement; cash of INR104.4 crore is available for acquisitions.
Uniware growth guidance of above 15% and Shipway above 20% from Q4 FY27 must be met to validate the outlook.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability recovery, with specific dated guidance for Shipway and Uniware. Cautious and evasive on realisation per transaction and ARPA trends, which management said are not like-for-like and not tracked, and on M&A timing, which it described as patient with no fixed timeline.
key_quotes: We remain confident of delivering more than 15% year-on-year revenue growth in Uniware from Quarter 4 FY27 onwards.
We are 50% more expensive than any other player in the market.
So hence, rate per transaction is not a metric that we anyway were proactively tracking within our business.
We will look at doing one only when we feel that all the four criteria that I laid down meet the bar for us.

growth.why: Management reiterated Uniware >15% and Shipway >20% revenue growth from Q4 FY27 and Shipway EBITDA breakeven from Q3 FY27, backed by 121 enterprise client adds (+17.5%) and module attach rates, but no specific capacity additions were disclosed and the margin outlook relies on moderating investment rather than concrete levers.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 17% from 22.2% YoY; management guided investment pace moderates in H2 FY27 and Shipway hits EBITDA break-even from Q3 FY27, with the long-term target of 20%+ at steady state.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Uniware guided to >15% revenue growth and Shipway to >20% from Q4 FY27, backed by 121 enterprise client adds in Q2 (+17.5%) and Q2 revenue up 15% YoY to INR59.1 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated existing guidance (Uniware >15%, Shipway >20%) without raising it, and ARPA is down about 5% YoY with a 520 bps margin compression.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 margin fell 520 bps to 17% and Shipway profitability depends partly on deferred tax recognition, so the Q3-Q4 recovery and Shipway break-even are not yet proven.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: DNA AI companion is in beta with 10-15 customers and offered free, with monetisation to follow; timing and pricing are unclear.

rows.label: ARPA stabilisation near INR2.4 lakh per quarter
rows.why: Quarterly ARPA fell to about INR2.4 lakh from INR2.9 lakh YoY (about -17%), driven by long-tail clients who take 6-9 months to ramp; management does not track it as a KPI, so stabilisation is unproven.

rows.label: UniReco and UniCapture attach to Uniware clients
rows.why: Run-rate exceeds INR3 crore (about 2.5% of Uniware revenue), with attach rates of 7-8% and 5-6%, and management expects these to exceed 10% of Uniware revenue over two to three years.

rows.label: M&A using INR104.4 crore cash
rows.why: Cash and bank balances rose 65% YoY to INR104.4 crore and management has signalled deals for several quarters, but gave no fixed timeline and set four criteria.

tone.note: Management was confident on Uniware and Shipway growth and Shipway break-even timing, but cautious and evasive on ARPA and per-transaction realisation (not tracked as like-for-like) and on M&A timing; analysts pushed on ARPA decline, the tech stack criticism and the deferred-tax-driven PAT.
